# Candidate sensor technologies
- Sensor-T1: thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
- Sensor-T3: planar sensor, standard pitch.
- Sensor-T2: 3D-electrode sensor, larger pitch.
All are qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

# Irradiation and test-beam campaign, 2026
Sensors were irradiated with reactor neutrons to 2e16 neq/cm^2 and measured at the SPS test beam.
Hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2:
- Sensor-T1: 82.0% (strong charge trapping; full depletion no longer reachable at the maximum bias)
- Sensor-T3: 98.5%
- Sensor-T2: 99.2%
Requirement for the innermost layer: >= 97% up to end of life.

# Meeting notes 2026-03-02
Cooling: CO2 evaporative cooling at -35 C confirmed. Mechanics: the carbon-fibre staves are on schedule.

# Readout chip
The common readout chip supports 50x50 um^2 pixels and a 1.5 GHz/cm^2 hit rate. All candidates are compatible.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 150 um, unirradiated)
Single-hit resolution: Sensor-T1 6.0 um, Sensor-T3 9.0 um, Sensor-T2 14.0 um.

input.justification: T1 has the best unirradiated resolution (6 um) but only 82% efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2, against a requirement of 97% or more. It is not suitable for the innermost layer. T3 and T2 both meet the requirement (98.5% and 99.2%). T3 has the better resolution of the two (9 um against 14 um), so I chose T3. I chose 150 um because that is the thickness the resolution simulation used. The documents don't say what thickness the irradiation efficiency was measured at, and they have no resolution or efficiency results for other thicknesses. T3's efficiency margin over the requirement is only 1.5 points, so the thickness should be checked with a dedicated irradiated-sensor study.

requirements.evidence: Among the technologies that pass the radiation requirement, T3 is best at 9 um (2025 simulation, 150 um, unirradiated). T2 is 14 um. T1 is 6 um but fails the radiation requirement. No post-irradiation resolution was available.
T3 measured 98.5% in the test beam and the query tool. T1 measured 82%.
